Hi Dana / Ravi — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and the proposed next steps focused on RAG/eval items we discussed so your engineering and data teams can evaluate model fit. I pasted a concise plan below and attached the prompt set + topline benchmark artifacts for your review.

Call highlights (30m):
- Primary use case: clinical note summarization + question answering over EHR-derived knowledgebase (internal policies and anonymized patient content).
- SLOs: median latency < 350ms for single-turn Q/A, recall-oriented grounding (precision for citations > 85% on our seed tests).
- Constraints: PHI-sensitive content (want VPC/private deployment), retention window 90 days, SOC2 required.

Recommended short evaluation program (2-3 weeks):
1) Retrieval baseline: dense retrieval with FAISS/ANN using chunk size 500 tokens; candidate_pool_top_k=100, rerank_top_n=10. Also test BM25 as a low-cost baseline.
2) Embedding model: run comparisons using open embeddings (text-embedding-3-small) vs your in-house tuned embeddings. Expect ~3-5% retrieval delta.
3) Reranker choices: start with a bi-encoder + light cross-encoder re‑rank (cross-encoder for top-10 only) — gives best precision/latency tradeoff. We recommend our 'cross-small' checkpoint for faster on-device scoring.
4) Generator model suggestions: test three variants: Redwood-7B-Quant (FP16/4bit), open-llama-13b-8k, and a safety-first smaller 3B model for guardrail checks.
5) Prompt & grounding evals: attached prompt suite (atlas_rag_prompt_suite_v1.xlsx) includes 30 canonical prompts, regression checks, and citation scoring rubric (PRec@K and grounding_confidence thresholds).

Benchmarks & links: benchmark_results_topline.csv (attached) and shared Drive folder with raw eval traces: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcBenchmarkResults

Compliance & deployment notes:
- For PHI: Private deployment (VPC) + KMS recommended. We'll include SOC2 evidence and audit logs in the next email.
- Data map and pseudonymization approach attached (data_map_pseudonymization.pdf).

Immediate next steps we propose:
- Your team: share a 200–500 doc sample (de‑identified) and identify one high-priority QA prompt set (choose 8–12 prompts).
- Our team: spin up a Dedicated eval sandbox, run retrieval + reranker variants, and return a topline report with PRec@1/3/5, citation precision, and latency percentiles.

Would Wednesday or Thursday next week work for a short triage to align on dataset handoff and access (1h)?

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Hi Dana — adding a few technical notes from the solutions side that should help with cost/latency tradeoffs and the retrieval tuning question: 

On retrieval K and chunking: 
- For clinical notes we typically chunk at 400–600 tokens with overlap 50–100 tokens to preserve context windows. We've seen PRec@1 flatten after ~120 candidates on dense vectors for similar datasets, but PRec@3 still improves up to 200 in edge cases. Our recommendation: run quick A/B at k=100 and k=200 for 1k queries to quantify ROI.

On cross-encoder latency: 
- Cross-encoder per-request latency depends on model size and deployment (dedicated GPU vs hosted). If you re-rank top-10 with a cross-small (optimized) model on a single T4-equivalent GPU, expect ~18–40ms per pair; end-to-end add of ~180–400ms for 10 candidates (batched scoring). That said, using a hybrid approach (light cross-encoder only for flagged low-confidence queries) reduces average added latency significantly.

Reranker suggestion: 
- Start with a bi-encoder vector search (Faiss/HNSW) then a distilled cross-encoder (we call 'xenc-distill-small') for top-10. If Atlas needs stricter grounding, bump to our 'xenc-standard'.

Quality/regression concerns & eval metrics: 
- Please pay special attention to citation precision (P@1/P@3), hallucination rate (manual review on a 200 sample), and grounding_confidence delta across model versions. We'll include regression alerts in Redwood Optimize so you can set thresholds.

I attached a compact prompt-suite (same file Diego attached) and a short script outline for computing PRec@K and grounding precision from the raw traces. If you want, Neha and I can watch the handoff call to fast-track the sandbox access.

Best,
